posts.title: Wet overnight, drying out
posts.body:
09/18/26 5:01am: Morning, its Friday. The sky out the window here is still overcast and the gauge caught a bit more overnight, which is the tail end of what came through.

Durango and the Animas Valley (6,500') are done with the wet stuff. The bus run should be dry and temps climbing through the 60s this morning. Clear sailing for anyone heading to town.

Bayfield and up the Pine (6,900') got a bit more overnight and could see a sprinkle or two through mid-morning, but nothing that changes the drive. The 501 should be fine for the school run, and districts decide by 6:30. Drying out through the day with temps in the upper 60s.

Vallecito and the Florida (7,650') caught the most overnight, about a third of an inch here at the house, and there's still a chance of light rain through the morning commute. The 240 could have some wet pavement early but nothing heavy. Should clear by afternoon with temps mid-60s.

The high Weminuche (10,500'+) is where the real action was, models showing close to an inch up top overnight and this morning. All rain though, the snow line has been sitting way above all of it and falling slowly. Any precip up there wraps by late morning.

For the passes, Coal Bank, Molas and Red Mountain could see some wet pavement early from overnight rain, mostly clearing through the morning. Wolf Creek same story. All rain at pass level, nothing frozen. Current road status and any restrictions: https://www.cotrip.org/

The SNOTEL at Vallecito is showing 4" of depth and 0.1" of SWE as of yesterday, which is that early-September snow from earlier in the week still sitting up there above 10,700'.

Drying trend holds through the weekend, then the GFS and Euro are hinting at another round of moisture early next week but they disagree on how much gets pulled north.

How's the 240 or the 501 looking on your drive this morning?

posts.title: Flood Watch for Vallecito, Bayfield and Durango
posts.body:
09/16/26 5:21am: The gauge here caught a little more overnight and its still drizzling, which is the setup for the bus run this morning.

Durango and the Animas Valley (6,500') woke up to light rain and should stay dry through the school run, then another round moves in tonight. I'd expect the 160 into town to be fine for the morning commute.

Bayfield and up the Pine (6,900') same story, a little overnight rain, and I'd expect nothing worse than damp pavement by the 6:30 call. The afternoon's a different deal but that's hours out.

Vallecito and up the Florida (7,650') caught a trace overnight and the 501 and the 240 should be dry for the morning run. Districts decide by 6:30 as always.

The snow line this morning is sitting way above the Weminuche (10,500'), so this is all rain everywhere. We're not talking about snow at the passes today.

Here's the thing though. The Grand Junction office has us under a Flood Watch through Thursday night, both COZ019 (Vallecito and up) and COZ022 (Durango and Bayfield). They're seeing moisture levels at 300% of normal and calling out the potential for extremely wet conditions Wednesday into Thursday. The NWS discussion mentions that soils are already saturated from the last couple days and there's not much room left for more water. That's the Flood Watch at https://weather.gov/gjt and you should read the whole thing.

The models are lining up on 1.5-2" of rain for most of us between now and Thursday night, with the worst of it coming tomorrow morning through tomorrow evening. Open-Meteo has Vallecito picking up 1.7" total through Thursday, Durango around 2". The Euro, GFS, ICON and GEM are all showing roughly the same setup so there's not much disagreement on this one. Take those totals with a grain of salt (the exact timing of the heaviest bands is still a little uncertain and that'll move the numbers around) but the pattern is solid.

Tonight into tomorrow is when this gets real. The heaviest rain looks like 6am to 6pm tomorrow, and that's when we'll see the highest risk for flash flooding and debris flows, especially in the burn scars and any of the drainages that've already been running high. The 416 scar and Missionary Ridge are both on the list.

This morning's fine. Tomorrow morning is the question.

What's the 501 or the 240 looking like on your end right now?

posts.title: Wet start, then Wednesday
posts.body:
09/15/26 5:35am: Tuesday, and the gauge finally has something in it after that overnight band, with the sky breaking up now.

Districts decide by 6:30. The 501 and the 240 should be wet but straightforward this morning after that early rain. Durango and Bayfield got a quick shot before sunrise, then it shut off. Way too warm for ice and the snow line is nowhere near us, so I'd expect wet pavement drying out as the sun gets to it.

Durango and the Animas Valley (6,500') are done with the morning moisture, clearing through the day with highs upper 70s to near 80. Dry afternoon, maybe an isolated storm late but nothing organized.

Bayfield and up the Pine (6,900') saw a trace to maybe 0.02" early, now clearing out. Same story, dry day, warm afternoon in the upper 70s.

Vallecito and the Florida (7,650') picked up around 0.17" in that early band, heavier than down low. Clearing now, dry through the afternoon and evening.

The high Weminuche (10,500'+) got around 0.3" early, all rain with the snow line nowhere near any of it. Clearing through midday.

Wednesday is the one to watch. The GJT discussion is pretty clear that Wednesday's the big day this week, with the best moisture, jet energy still overhead, and a shortwave moving through. Open-Meteo is showing Durango picking up over an inch Wednesday afternoon and evening, Vallecito around 0.5-0.7", and the high country over 2" of liquid. That's a lot. Take those amounts with a big grain of salt (the models have been all over the place with timing and placement this week), but Wednesday afternoon into evening looks like a soaker. Snow line stays well above all of it, so its all rain even up top.

Today takes care of itself. Wednesday is the one I'd move plans around for.

The passes should be wet early from that overnight rain, then drying through the morning. Coal Bank, Molas and Red Mountain all stayed rain at pass level. Wolf Creek same story. Current closures and chain law: https://www.cotrip.org/

Anybody up the Florida get more than a third of an inch out of that?

posts.title: Dry drive, then afternoon storms
posts.body:
09/14/26 6:33am: Clear sky over the house and the gauge is empty, and thats the easy part of today.

Districts decide by 6:30 and I'd expect a straightforward morning drive across the county. Durango and Bayfield should stay dry through the school run, and the 501 and the 240 should be no trouble. Vallecito and up the Florida same story, should be dry pavement for the early run.

The afternoon is the question. Models are setting up scattered storms starting around 2pm, strongest between 2pm and 5pm, which puts them right in the pickup window. The GFS, Euro, ICON and GEM all show the same setup: afternoon convection with some cells capable of heavy rain in short bursts, gusty wind, and maybe some small hail. The NWS discussion out of Grand Junction is pointing at a corridor from southeastern Utah toward the Grand Mesa as the best spot for stronger storms, with the expectation that things stratify out as they move east over the San Juans. Embedded heavier cells are still possible even in that scenario.

Snow line is way above anything we live at or drive over, so this is all rain everywhere today. Durango and the Animas Valley could see a third of an inch through the afternoon, Bayfield and up the Pine maybe half an inch with the heavier cells, Vallecito and the Florida a tenth to a quarter inch depending on which storms track through. The high Weminuche could pick up close to half an inch between afternoon and overnight, all rain above 10,500 feet.

The 550 passes should turn wet through the afternoon, mostly rain at pass level even up at Red Mountain. Wolf Creek same deal. Forecast only, current road status is at cotrip.org.

After the afternoon round clears out we get another push overnight into Tuesday morning, lighter and more scattered. Then another round Tuesday evening. The pattern holds through the end of the week, southwest flow aloft keeping moisture around and afternoon storms in the forecast every day.

Did the morning drive give you anything different than this?

posts.title: Dry today, watching Monday
posts.body:
09/13/26 6:51am: Sunday, and the gauge hasnt caught a thing. Clear sky and dry ground if youre headed out to the lake or running errands in town today.

Durango and the Animas Valley stay dry through the day. Temps push into the low 80s this afternoon with some wind picking up, gusts 15-25 by evening. There's a small chance of an isolated shower late but I wouldn't count on it.

Bayfield and up the Pine, same deal. Clear morning, warm afternoon, breezy by evening. Any shower activity stays scattered and light if it shows up at all.

Vallecito and up the Florida Road, you're looking at the same dry setup through tonight. Tomorrow's a different story though, and I'll get to that in a second.

The high Weminuche stays dry today but the wind picks up this afternoon, gusts 15-25 up top.

Now, tonight into tomorrow is where things get interesting. A deep trough drops into the Pacific Northwest and the models are all showing a strong push of subtropical moisture getting pulled inland. The GFS is the only one showing a trace for Vallecito (0.03"), the Euro, ICON and GEM keep us dry, but the setup favors tomorrow for the real event. Precipitable water values are forecast to hit 200% of normal, which is way up there for mid-September. The snow line tonight is way above anything we live at or drive over, so this is all rain for us, but it could be heavy rain. The NWS discussion mentions the potential for cell training and localized flash flooding tomorrow, especially with that cold front pushing through tonight. I'm watching that setup closely and I'll have a full breakdown tomorrow morning.

The 550 passes should stay dry today and turn wet tonight, all rain at pass level with that line as high as it is. Same for Wolf Creek, rain right through it, no snow in this one. That's the forecast, current road status is at cotrip.org.

Anyone getting out on the water today or up on a trail?

posts.title: Morning forecast for Vallecito, Bayfield and Durango
posts.body:
09/11/26 5:04am: Friday morning, and theres still not a drop on the woodpile. Dry is the whole story for the county today.

The bus run should be straightforward this morning. Durango and the Animas Valley start in the upper 50s and climb to the mid-80s this afternoon. Bayfield and up the Pine start low 50s and track the same pattern. Vallecito and the Florida start mid-50s, then push into the low 80s by afternoon.

All the models agree we stay dry through the day. The Euro, GFS, ICON and GEM all show zero precipitation through tonight and tomorrow, so theres no disagreement to hedge. A few afternoon clouds maybe, but nothing that develops.

Wind picks up this afternoon, gusts to 20-25mph in town and Bayfield, a bit less up the Florida. The high Weminuche stays breezy through the day, gusts 15-25 up there.

The 550 north should stay dry over Coal Bank, Molas and Red Mountain through the day. I'd expect Wolf Creek on the 160 to run the same. That's the forecast, not the road status, so check CDOT for current conditions and chain law: https://www.cotrip.org/

Districts decide by 6:30 as usual and I'd expect a clean drive in this morning.

Vallecito's still sitting at 22% of full pool and the SNOTEL up there is showing 0.1" SWE with 3" of depth, which is just trace stuff from whatever blew through earlier this week.

The Grand Junction discussion is watching SubTrop moisture trying to work north into the Four Corners this weekend, so things could get more interesting Saturday and Sunday, but today stays quiet.

I'll have more later if anything changes.

posts.title: Morning forecast for Vallecito, Bayfield and Durango
posts.body:
09/10/26 5:06am: Second morning running I havent had to wipe the windshield, and that tells you most of what today holds.

Durango and the Animas Valley should see a straightforward morning, then a warm afternoon pushing near 90 under sun. Light winds early, gusts 15-25 this afternoon. Tomorrow looks similar, just a tick cooler with a slim rain chance late in the day that I dont think amounts to much.

Bayfield and up the Pine, same setup. Clear start, warming through the 80s, breezy this afternoon with gusts 18-28. Tomorrow stays dry through the school run, with that same low-end pop showing up in the models for late afternoon Friday.

Vallecito and up the Florida, youre looking at mid-50s this morning and low 80s this afternoon. Winds lighter than down valley, 10-19mph gusts. Tomorrow morning stays clear for the early drive, with Friday afternoon showing a sliver of a rain chance that all four models agree is basically nothing.

The high Weminuche sits in the upper 40s this morning and climbs to near 70 this afternoon. Breezy up top both days, gusts 20-30 Friday afternoon.

The passes should stay dry through today and tomorrow morning. Coal Bank, Molas and Red Mountain should all be clear for the early runs, and I'd expect Wolf Creek to be the same. For current road status and chain law: https://www.cotrip.org/

The SNOTEL at Vallecito is sitting at 0.1" SWE and 4" depth, which is trace stuff from earlier in the week. The Animas at Durango is running 153 cfs.

The Grand Junction discussion has us under building high pressure with zonal flow keeping things dry through Friday. They're watching a moisture push for the weekend, but theres disagreement on timing and whether any frontal boundary holds together enough to actually fire anything. The ECENS is later and weaker than the GEFS, and the forcing question is still open. More on that tomorrow as it tightens up.

Anybody else already thinking about when this heat breaks?

posts.title: Morning forecast for Vallecito, Bayfield and Durango
posts.body:
09/09/26 5:09am: The gauge stayed dry overnight and the morning drive down the 501 should be straightforward.

Districts decide by 6:30 as always, but there's nothing in the weather to slow anybody down this morning. Durango and Bayfield both start cool (mid-50s to near 60F) and warm fast into the low-to-mid 80s this afternoon. Clear all day, light winds early, picking up a bit this afternoon but nothing that'll cause trouble.

Up the Pine and around Vallecito we're starting in the upper 50s and topping out low 80s. Same deal, dry through the day. Pop values tick up a hair late afternoon but that's just the models acknowledging September exists, not a real chance at anything.

The high country woke up around 50F and gets into the upper 60s today. Still dry up there, winds picking up a bit through the afternoon (gusts to 18-19mph) but nothing dramatic.

The passes should stay dry all day. Coal Bank, Molas and Red Mountain get light winds early, a bit gustier this afternoon, but no weather. Wolf Creek the same. For current road status check https://www.cotrip.org/ before you head out.

All four models (Euro, GFS, ICON, GEM) agree we stay bone dry through tomorrow, and GJ's discussion has us staying that way through Thursday. They're watching Friday for a possible moisture push depending on how a trough off the Pacific Northwest tracks, but that's still days out and the setup's uncertain.

The Vallecito SNOTEL's still showing that trace from last week (0.1" SWE, 3" depth) but everything else is at zero. Animas at Durango running 165 cfs, Los Pinos above the lake at 26 cfs.

What's the morning looking like at your place?
